title: You're Shorter Tonight Than This Morning
takeaway: The soft discs between your spine bones get squashed by gravity all day, so you are about 1 cm shorter by night; lying down overnight lets them refill. Without gravity, astronauts grow up to about 3% taller (around 5 cm).
lines: see lines.json (captions) and tts.json (text with audio tags sent to ElevenLabs)
sources: https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/astronauts-get-taller-in-space/ (astronauts grow up to 3 percent taller; spine discs expand without gravity)
https://indianapublicmedia.org/amomentofscience/tall/ (taller in the morning, discs compress during the day)
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24099165/ (field study of daily spinal shrinkage)
pacing_brief: Hook = Battery's panicked true claim (a whole centimetre shorter than this morning) in the first second on a close shot of the door-frame marks. 30.7 s, 7 lines, ~16 shots: cut on every line, 3-part science insert (cute disc faces between bones -> sun crosses the sky while the discs flatten next to a sponge crushed by books -> night, asleep in bed with an x-ray strip as discs puff back up), space insert with Battery as an astronaut stretching taller, punch-in on 'tall', cut mid-L6 to the two-shot. Natural speed (Kalu atempo 1.06), tight gaps. Abrupt end on Battery's deflated face after 'before breakfast' (loops to the morning mark).
